# Amin opening and frontier audit

Audited all six original V14-family histories (V10, V10-v6, V14; cases1/2), decisions0–199 and observation200. This is one consumed competition1v1 placement with mirrors, not FFA evidence. No policy inference, engine replay or new games. The doctrine is bound as an input; construction is included.

## Tick income and retention

Each table cell is **our land/army : opponent land/army; exact retained plain1→2 tiles**. Every counted1→2 cell was untouched by either applied action on the tick transition, making the observed growth attribution unambiguous.

| Observation | V10 | V10-v6 | V14 |
|---|---|---|---|
|50|14/40 :19/45;11|same|same|
|100|43/108 :41/111;38|same|same|
|150|64/191 :55/185;45|72/198 :54/183;48|same asV10|
|200|75/228 :70/217;36|70/228 :71/214;13|same counts asV10|

Growth occurs on the transition into observation50/100/150/200, after actions49/99/149/199. Whole-land production and structure production are separate. All three have no castles and **zero affordable legal BUILD opportunities in these200 decisions** under the actual cost35+own-structure proximity surcharge. This does not establish that an earlier construction-oriented trajectory is bad: that alternative was not simulated.

Before50,13 actual captures remain owned continuously through the tick; before100,29 do. In100–149 V10/V14 retain21/21 capture events, V10-v6 retains29/29. In150–199 V10 retains22/28, V14 retains22/29, and V10-v6 retains only6/20. These are capture events, including possible recaptures, not unique independent tiles. V10-v6's extra immediate expansion at150 does not yield better retained frontier income at200.

Exact1→2 cells' mean Manhattan distance from home grows from3.64 at50 to10.42 at100 and16.62 at150 for V10/V14 (V10-v6:15.46 at150). This is a long attack-line footprint, not compact home growth. Manhattan distance is geometric locality; the per-frame evidence also records shortest currently-owned route distance to each alternative's source, without treating unknown terrain as known.

## Available moves versus deployable options

There is at least one legal, affordable, visible neutral-plain **full-move** capture on198/200 frames. That headline includes draining the capital below its own policy reserve and must not be read as198 safe opportunities. Enumerating full and half moves while requiring a home-source move to leave the original parent's `general_reserve` reduces availability to182 frames. No chosen PASS has a reserve-preserving alternative; the early passes are a negative control against indiscriminate expansion.

Of those182 frames, a different action is chosen106 times by V10/V14 and108 by V10-v6. After excluding actually issued protected offense and explicit urgent-defense decisions,70 V10,72 V14 and107 V10-v6 frames remain. These are opportunities for scrutiny, not proven mistakes: campaign movement can scout, assemble force, conceal home or prepare later captures. Current offensive-packet/defender-source flags and nearest visible-enemy distance are retained for each option. Parent reserve compliance is not a proof of safety under fog.

First visible hostile contact is128 in all three runs. One invisible-enemy frame later would not reset that contact. No inference is made about whether the opponent has seen us.

## Earliest concrete opportunity and a sharper boundary case

At16, all three policies choose half home5 south into already-owned(9,17). Half NORTH to observed neutral0 at(7,17) is also legal, leaves the same home3 reserve, and captures a home-adjacent tile immediately. There is no visible contact or protected offense/explicit defense. However, the actual south packet continues through owned(10,17) and captures new land on18–19. Replacing16 is a real tradeoff between immediate local income and an advancing line; it is not a free extra tile or a proven win.

At49, the parent instead transfers7 from(14,16) south into owned(15,16). Its next capture is on50, arriving after the land tick. Meanwhile half home6 NORTH would capture the still-neutral(7,17), leave home3, and—if it executes and survives—qualify that tile for imminent tick50. The north tile is never captured in the original V10 history. This is the smallest discriminating timing fixture: a reserved, observed local capture immediately before production versus a remote transfer whose capture lies after production. It needs an adaptive continuation to measure the displaced route, survival and home exposure; it has not earned a benefit claim here.

At27 there is also a non-home alternative: the packet at(11,17) could capture neutral(11,16) instead of transferring south. This avoids the simple home-drain objection but may redirect the useful southward line. The evidence retains both full/half actions, residual armies and locality; no threshold was fitted to later results.

## Do not destroy productive contact plans

At129 there are14 nominal full-move neutral options, including a2-army nearby donor at(8,15) able to capture(7,15). V10 instead begins its real four-action concentration, capturing enemy(14,10) on132. At142 its eight-action plan captures enemy(13,10) on149, **before** tick150. These are actual productive attack plans, not mere repeated transfers. A rule that always substitutes a cheap neutral capture would interrupt them, including a useful capture exactly at the production boundary. Their protection should be tested explicitly.

The contrasting V10-v6 path takes immediate neutral expansion and reaches72land at150 versus64, but later retains only6 of20 capture events through200 and loses this complete game at370. This falsifies treating short-term land count alone as sufficient strength evidence. V10 wins at1033 and V14 loses524; these later outcomes are contextual controls, not effects causally attributed to any opening alternative in this audit.

## Bounded next hypothesis

Before established contact, compare a currently visible reserve-preserving local capture's next-tick eligibility against the selected campaign transfer's concrete route progress. Keep the comparison subordinate to current explicit defense and actually issued attack plans after contact, and retain a measure of the displaced packet's next useful capture. The16/27/49 observations are distinct test cases;129/142 and the early reserve-bound passes are negative controls. Evaluate actual retained tick income, home exposure and completed line progress, not proposed moves or a service counter. Construction remains in scope, but no currently legal opening BUILD was available in these histories.

`report.json` and six200-row JSONL files contain the full census. `reserve-report.json` supplies split/reserve-aware alternatives and exact selected cases. Helpers, reports, doctrine, rules and original source/raw inputs are hashed in `manifest.json`; both numerical commands exited0. Legal alternatives are pre-action public-state assessments, not assertions that they would execute unchanged against adaptive future opponent actions.

frontier-audit-external.report:
# V15 recorded opening frontier audit

Completed six original first-200 candidate histories: V10, V10-v6, and V14 on Juraj V3.5 case12 and my_bot9 case4. All six full mirrored histories (cases15/7) match after player-label normalization in public wires, applied actions, and incoming/returned candidate memory. This is a public-wire NumPy census, not policy inference, changed-state simulation, or new matches. Original completion/strict-check/source-freeze evidence and all twelve frame files are hash-bound in report.json. The preserved public fixtures retain the exact original key and incoming memory.

## What the opening actually buys

All three policies use the same first50-action breakdown on both placements: 12 passes, 22 owned transfers, and 16 successful neutral-plain captures. At observation50 each owns17land/43army. Juraj reaches19land/45army with 24passes, eight transfers, and18neutral captures. Equal action count does not imply equal production: the current opening spends considerably more actions transporting small armies.

Public observation counts below are our land/army versus opponent land/army. Values refer to observations after the named production tick, not the prior action.

| Placement / policy | 50 | 100 | 150 | 200 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Juraj V10 | 17/43 vs19/45 | 36/86 vs38/90 | 42/118 vs51/131 | 42/147 vs69/187 |
| Juraj V10-v6 | 17/43 vs19/45 | 36/86 vs38/90 | 55/142 vs56/147 | 67/202 vs65/205 |
| Juraj V14 | 17/43 vs19/45 | 36/86 vs38/90 | 42/120 vs51/133 | 52/164 vs60/185 |
| my_bot9 V10 | 17/43 vs17/43 | 24/65 vs31/72 | 35/98 vs27/97 | 52/141 vs26/78 |
| my_bot9 V10-v6 | 17/43 vs17/43 | 24/67 vs33/76 | 32/98 vs31/106 | 46/129 vs22/82 |
| my_bot9 V14 | 17/43 vs17/43 | 24/65 vs31/72 | 42/105 vs32/102 | 47/129 vs35/114 |

At tick50, each policy/placement has14 plain tiles observed owned1→owned2 with neither player's preceding action touching them. On Juraj, all14 depart within the next50 observations: ten first reinforce owned land, four first capture neutral land. Eleven remain continuously owned throughout observations50–99. On my_bot9, eleven depart: five transfer, six capture neutral; three do not depart in that window. Continuous ownership retention is10/14 for V10/V14 and13/14 for V10-v6. These subsets deliberately omit other real income (larger garrisons, structures, action-touched tiles, and newly captured tiles). Tick100/150/200 per-cell income and retention are retained in report.json.

## Neutral alternatives remain available

The census accepts only currently visible type1/plain, owner0 destinations with strictly sufficient moving army. It does not mistake fog0 or ambiguous structures for neutral land. Each source-destination full move is counted once; half affordability is separately recorded.

A descriptive screen filter excludes the general, the recorded defender/target reservation, and sources with any currently visible enemy in their3×3 neighborhood. It is NOT a home-route safety proof. Every Juraj owned transfer in100–199 has an affordable alternative passing this filter. Thus lack of visible neutral opportunities does not explain the missed expansion.

| Placement / policy | 100–149 transfer / neutral / enemy attempts | 150–199 transfer / neutral / enemy attempts |
|---|---|---|
| Juraj V10 | 31 / 4 / 15 | 33 / 2 / 15 |
| Juraj V10-v6 | 22 / 17 / 11 | 29 / 5 / 16 |
| Juraj V14 | 34 / 4 / 12 | 28 / 2 / 20 |
| my_bot9 V10 | 36 / 2 / 12 | 29 / 13 / 8 |
| my_bot9 V10-v6 | 40 / 0 / 10 | 28 / 2 / 20 |
| my_bot9 V14 | 28 / 7 / 15 | 29 / 7 / 14 |

The Juraj V10-v6 17neutral attempts include16 next-observation confirmed captures; every other neutral attempt in this table succeeds under that definition. For V14 Juraj, alternatives coexist with12 actually issued collection frames in100–149 and13 in150–199. Nineteen and eleven transfer frames respectively also exclude ongoing offense/direct-start and the descriptive defense flags. These are recorded-state opportunities, not a predicted intervention count after a policy changes history.

No candidate builds or attempts a neutral/enemy castle in these first200 actions. This sample diagnoses plain expansion and transport, not castle investment quality.

## Earliest interventions and their real tradeoff

At turn17 in both placements, all policies transport an own3 packet between owned cells while a visible empty neutral neighbor is available from that same non-home source.

* Juraj: actual (9,17)→(10,17); alternative east to(9,18), two terrain steps from home. The destination has two other visible neutral-plain neighbors and no blocked in-bounds onward neighbor. It remains uncaptured throughout the original V14 episode.
* my_bot9: actual (13,5)→(12,5); alternative west to(13,4), also two steps from home, with two visible neutral onward neighbors plus one unknown neighbor. The original V14 does not capture it until143.

These are plausible local-expansion starting fixtures, not demonstrated improvements. The actual transfer is productive too: on each map it feeds two confirmed neutral captures on18/19, each retained for at least50 subsequent observations. A neutral-first action with the same3army can fund two serial empty-tile captures, but it changes the exploration direction and future feeder route. Do not label every transfer wasted solely because a capture exists.

The sharper phase-boundary opportunity is my_bot9 turn49: own5 at(11,5) transfers east into owned(11,6), while west(11,4) is visible empty neutral with two visible onward neutral neighbors. Capturing before the action49→observation50 transition would qualify that tile for the imminent land increment, if retained. The original capture occurs only145. This is a timing/legality observation, not an adaptive outcome claim.

After growth, Juraj turn54 offers fourteen screened capture options while the actual action halves home12 into the feeder route. Own2 at(9,17) can instead capture(9,18), or own2 at(8,16) can capture(7,16). my_bot9 turn56 offers own2 at(13,5)→(13,4) while another packet transfers toward the active front. Such independent small donors avoid spending a large offensive packet, but their use still consumes the single global action and delays something else.

## Productive hazards a new frontier policy must preserve

* my_bot9 turn64 is an actual ready direct capture: own6 at(3,6) attacks enemy1 at(2,6), leaving4 and retaining the destination for at least50 observations. An affordable neutral alternative exists elsewhere. Neutral availability must not replace this direct action automatically.
* Juraj turn79 moves an11army packet toward contact despite available nearby neutral captures. The initial objective changes on80–81, but the recorded packet reaches two enemy captures on83/84, both retained at least50 observations. This is evidence of productive transport across updated plans, not a claim that the original plan remains uninterrupted or optimal.
* The strongest aggregate counterexample in this selected set is my_bot9 V10-v6: it wins296 despite40 transfers and zero neutral attempts during100–149. The proposed frontier module must not treat neutral-action rate as the objective or indiscriminately interrupt this offensive route.
* No genuine threatened-home response occurs in these first200 candidate frames. The four flagged early observations0–3 reflect the inherited minimum reserve before initial expansion, with no screened neutral alternative. Therefore these openings cannot validate urgent-defense preservation; that needs existing tactical fixtures or dedicated tests.

## Minimal discrimination for implementation

Test an explicit low-force visible-neutral action choice at opening/land-production opportunities, scored for action cost, known onward frontier, production timing, and public threat exposure. Favor using independent2–3army donors over stripping a traveling attack packet; preserve actual direct captures, winning attacks, active defensive reservations, and coherent ongoing offensive transport. The appropriate production service event is a confirmed useful acquisition, not another owned transfer.

Turn17 is the earliest plausible intervention on these two states; my_bot9 turn49 and the post-tick54/56 fixtures distinguish timing and independent-donor behavior. The packet/capture counterexamples above must remain controls. Do not tune a universal home-radius or neutral quota from two placements. Full adaptive games are required to find out whether a production frontier can recover Juraj's economic gap while retaining my_bot9 and Amin pressure.

All metrics are conditional on original history. No later result is attributed causally to an isolated action; no hypothetical hidden enemy is used in candidate filters. Locality uses current known terrain, permitting uncertain ordinary fog as potential terrain only; it is not an oracle route or ownership claim. Source policies and original evidence were not edited.

manifest.scope: No policy/engine inference, no matches, no tracked edits. Six first200 episodes; six full mirror pairs. All original public records remain unchanged.

limitations: Available legal moves are counterfactual opportunities, not proven improvements.
One-army-tile production census uses untouched retained plains to avoid action/growth attribution ambiguity.
Short-term land alone does not establish superiority.
Current aggregated enemy observation cannot implement distinct FFA contacts.
